intent: Test whether a finer sensor array fixes the s-bend and slalom max_error plateau at about 0.062. Keep the iteration-7 design (y 0.05 m, 0.016 m footprint, track 0.10 m, body 0.10 x 0.12 m, mass 0.5 kg) and change only the sensor count and spacing: seven sensors from x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.0267 m spacing. Target: s-bend and slalom progress above 0.19, max_error below 0.062 m, oval finish rate at or above 65%, and oval steering_oscillation below 0.25.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) The s-bend and slalom max_error plateau comes from centre-line resolution at 0.04 m spacing, so a 0.027 m array lowers max_error and raises their progress. (2) The extra sensors add a little noise to the weighted signal, so oval steering_oscillation may rise slightly, but it should stay under 0.25. (3) If s-bend and slalom progress stay at about 0.14 and 0.19 with max_error unchanged, the plateau is turn response or controller-side, not sensing. The next geometry lever is then wheel_track 0.11 m, with mass 0.5 kg held. Please report per-track progress, max_error and steering_oscillation, and the oval finish rate.
rationale: The best raced design is still iteration 7 (score 315.27), which iteration 9 reverted to. Its design is body 0.10 x 0.12 m, track 0.10 m, mass 0.5 kg, 0.016 m footprints, and five sensors at y 0.05 m spanning x = -0.08 to 0.08 m. The evidence since then points away from mass and sensor lead. Iteration 8 (y 0.03 m) cut slalom progress from 0.186 to 0.075 and oval finish from 75% to 40%, so the shorter lead is ruled out. Iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg) lowered s-bend progress to 0.140 with no slalom gain, so mass is not the limit. Sensing is no longer the limit either: line loss is near zero on the s-bend and slalom (0 and 0.2 events), and the oval finish rate is 75%. Yet s-bend and slalom still end off_track at max_error about 0.062 to 0.064, with progress of 0.14 and 0.186. The Integrator's conditional for this case is met: max_error stays at about 0.062 with progress below 0.2 at y 0.05 m. Their stated next step is a 7-sensor array at x = -0.08 to 0.08 with 0.027 m spacing, keeping the 0.016 m footprint and y 0.05 m. I adopt that. Seven sensors give a finer centre-line signal, so the robot can see the tape's edge earlier on the bends. The span, footprint, lead, track, body, wheel radius and mass are all unchanged, so the race isolates the array density. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error falls below 0.062 and their progress rises above about 0.19, while the oval finish rate holds at 75% or better. Risk: the extra sensors may add noise or change the signal scale, which would show up as higher oval oscillation. If the score falls below about 300 or the oval finish rate drops below 65%, the next step is to revert to the five-sensor iteration 7 geometry.
